§6Boron

§aNeutron-absorbing metalloid that makes reactors controllable and the ZIRNOX possible.

§bBoron§f (atomic 5) is a bluish-grey metalloid whose neutron-absorbing properties make it essential for reactor control.

§6Production§f (no dedicated ore, mostly byproducts):
• Process §brare earth ore§f in anvil for boron fragments
• Centrifuge §bcoal ash§f for tiny piles
• Acidize §bborax§f with sulfuric acid (most efficient)
• Electrolyze §brare earth crystals§f or §blithium crystals§f for larger quantities
• Cyclotron: beryllium + lithium or vice versa

§6Key Uses§f:
• §bRBMK Neutron Absorbers§f, 8 ingots around structural column
• §bZIRNOX Reactor§f, requires 8 boron ingots
• §bRBMK Console§f and Crane Console
• Chicago Pile and PWR control rods
• Boron glass for RBMK cover panels

§ePS:§f Boron is relatively abundant as a byproduct. Centrifuge your coal ash and rare earth chunks instead of mining for it.
